iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system has exactly 6 active inputs (X1-X6) and 6 inert inputs (X7-X12). The Pareto-optimal surface fixes X1=1, X3=1, X4=1, X5≥0.55 (saturated) and is parameterized by X2∈[0.1,1] and X6∈[0.1,1] as trade-off variables. X2 controls the (Y1+Y4) vs Y2 trade-off: higher X2 increases Y1, Y4, and Y2. X6 controls the Y1 vs Y4 trade-off at roughly fixed Y2 (at high X2, X6 actually decreases Y2, a sign-reversal interaction). Y3 is controlled by X1 and X3 with strong synergy and always satisfies Y3≥0.4 at X1=X3=1. Strong super-additive multi-way interactions inflate Y1 at extreme configurations. The X6 effect on Y1 is highly convex (accelerating at high X6). My model is well-calibrated in the optimization region (X1=X3=1) with errors <0.01, but poorly calibrated at moderate X1/X3 values where Y2 is much higher than predicted (error 0.22 at calibration point).
new_findings: Calibration check revealed my Y2 model is severely wrong outside the X1=X3=1 region: predicted Y2=0.19 but actual was 0.41 (error=0.22). X1 and X3 have much stronger nonlinear Y2-reducing effects than captured by linear gradients.
Y3 model is also inaccurate at moderate X1/X3: predicted 0.22 vs actual 0.38, suggesting the X1*X3 relationship is not purely multiplicative but has additive components.
Y1 and Y4 predictions remain excellent even at non-optimal configs (errors -0.016 and -0.002), confirming those output models are robust.
The Pareto front has 31 non-dominated points with HV=0.2645, all on the X1=X3=X4=1, X5=0.7 surface varying X2 and X6.
The X6 effect on Y1 is highly convex: at X2=1.0, the first 0.2 step in X6 (0.1→0.3) adds only 0.009 to Y1, while the last 0.25 step (0.75→1.0) adds 0.078.
surprises: Y2 calibration error of 0.22 was the biggest surprise. At X1=0.31, X3=0.43, Y2=0.41 instead of predicted 0.19. This means X1 and X3 reduce Y2 nonlinearly - their effect is much larger than OAT gradients at the base config suggested. Possibly a threshold or exponential relationship.

Y3 calibration error of 0.16 shows the X1*X3→Y3 model needs refinement. At X1=0.31, X3=0.43, Y3=0.38 vs multiplicative prediction of ~0.13. There must be significant additive/offset terms in the Y3 model.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: With 6 evals remaining, fill the largest gaps in the Pareto front grid: (1) X2=0.9 at X6={0.3, 0.55, 0.75} to complete the X2=0.9 row across all X6 levels, (2) X2=0.65 at X6={0.1, 0.3, 0.55} to fill the largest Y1/Y2 gaps between X2=0.55 and X2=0.775. These 6 points should densify the Pareto surface and improve hypervolume.

iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system has exactly 6 active inputs (X1-X6) and 6 inert inputs (X7-X12). The Pareto-optimal surface fixes X1=1, X3=1, X4=1, X5=0.7 (above saturation threshold ~0.55) and is parameterized by X2∈[0.1,1] and X6∈[0.1,1] as the two trade-off variables. X2 controls the (Y1+Y4) vs Y2 trade-off: higher X2 increases Y1, Y4, and Y2 simultaneously. X6 controls the Y1 vs Y4 trade-off: higher X6 increases Y1 but decreases Y4, and at high X2 it actually decreases Y2 (sign-reversal interaction). Y3 is controlled exclusively by X1×X3 with strong multiplicative synergy plus an additive offset, and always satisfies Y3≥0.4 when X1=X3=1. Strong super-additive multi-way interactions (X2×X4, X2×X6, X1×X3) inflate Y1 far beyond additive predictions at extreme configurations. The X6 effect on Y1 is highly convex (accelerating at high X6). The model is extremely well-calibrated in the optimization region with max prediction error <0.004 across 20+ predictions, but poorly calibrated at moderate X1/X3 values where nonlinear Y2-reducing effects of X1 and X3 are much stronger than linear gradients suggest (error 0.22 at one calibration point). The 36-point Pareto front achieves HV=0.2662 with best values Y1=1.131, Y2=0.071, Y4=0.322, and Y3=0.997 everywhere on the front.
new_findings: All 5 final Pareto-filling evaluations had prediction errors <0.004 across all outputs, confirming the bilinear interpolation model is extremely accurate in the optimization region.
Adding X2=0.9 at X6={0.3, 0.55, 0.75} and X2=0.65 at X6={0.1, 0.55} densified the Pareto front from 31 to 36 non-dominated points and improved hypervolume from 0.2645 to 0.2662.
All 5 new points were non-dominated, confirming the 2D (X2, X6) grid is the correct parameterization of the Pareto surface.

The calibration check at a sub-optimal point (X1=0.86, X3=0.82, X4=0.58) revealed Y1 overestimation of 0.13, confirming super-additive interactions cause Y1 to drop faster than linearly when multiple inputs move below their optima.
Y2, Y3, Y4 predictions at the calibration point were excellent (errors <0.04), showing those output models are more robust to input perturbations than the Y1 model.
surprises: The calibration point Y1 error of -0.13 was notable: at X1=0.86, X3=0.82, X4=0.58 (all sub-optimal), Y1=0.359 vs predicted 0.49. The super-additive interactions mean that when MULTIPLE inputs simultaneously decrease from optimal, Y1 drops much faster than predicted by independent marginal effects. This is consistent with the multi-way interaction structure identified earlier.

Despite the Y1 calibration error at sub-optimal configs, the optimization-region predictions remained perfect (<0.004 error), confirming the model is highly accurate where it matters most for Pareto optimization.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: Budget exhausted (144/144 evals used). If more budget were available, I would: (1) Fill remaining gaps at X2=0.2 with X6={0.3, 0.55, 0.75} and X2=0.65 with X6={0.3, 0.75, 1.0} to complete the Pareto grid, (2) Test whether X5 values slightly above 0.55 (e.g. 0.6) give identical results to X5=0.7 to confirm saturation, (3) Explore whether slight reductions in X4 (e.g. 0.85) with compensating X2/X6 adjustments could yield new non-dominated points.
